$comment: Adjudicated non-defects for db/gates/check-league-schema-consumers.mjs.
Every entry is keyed on a SITE -- (path, table, column) for gate 1, or
(path, statement_contains) for gate 2 -- and NEVER on a column name alone.
Judging per (table, column) is the difference between fixing and breaking:
pff_player_seasonlogs.pff_id survives while player.pff_id does not, and
scoring_format_player_seasonlogs.year survives while player_seasonlogs.year
does not. A name-keyed entry here would be the stoplist that hid a real
defect in check-renamed-column-consumers, which returned 129 findings with
not one of them `total` over a rename that wiped a year of projection values.
An entry that no longer suppresses anything is reported as a FINDING, so a
repaired or deleted site forces its entry out rather than leaving a standing
exemption. Do not add an entry to quiet a gate you have not read.
kind = history      accurate past-tense record of what a rename DID; only
live instruction counts as a defect
kind = not_a_column the token is a real thing that is not a database column
(a config key, a JS property, a spec basename, a value)
kind = pending_ruling  the SQL is genuinely broken and its INTENT is ambiguous,
so no repair can be chosen without an operator ruling.
Unlike the kinds above this does NOT assert the site is
correct -- it records that the finding is real, understood,
and parked on a decision. State the decision being awaited.
kind = fragment     a documented block that continues a structure an EARLIER
block defined, so it names a relation that is real in the
doc's narrative and absent from any schema. Record which
block defines it, so the entry falls when that one moves.

adjudications.reason: Real 42883 (character varying <> integer), surfaced only after the o_am -> over_american_odds repair removed the 42703 that was masking it. props_index.prop_type was a numeric enum when this query was written and became a string vocabulary in league 0221a941b; the live 2023 values are names (GAME_RECEIVING_YARDS, GAME_RUSHING_YARDS, ...) with no numeric codes at all. So quoting it as '18' would turn a loud type error into a predicate that matches NOTHING and silently widens the result set -- the bound-value-type class this repo already records for .where('public', true) against a smallint. Repairing it needs the one fact not recoverable from the schema or the pre-rename constants: which prop type the legacy code 18 named. Awaiting that; then replace the literal and remove this entry. The sibling file prop-recent-hits.sql carried no such predicate and is fully repaired.

Operator ruling 2026-08-18, relayed via the league management session: the 2023 week archives under text/nfl-betting are HISTORY and stay as is. They are the record of what was actually run at the time, so rewriting them to satisfy a later conform would destroy the thing they exist to preserve. Every failure in this file is the same 42702 -- an unqualified season_year predicate that was unambiguous when written and became ambiguous once a joined table was conformed to the same name, which is the rename-makes-a-predicate-ambiguous class. The entry is keyed on the file's one statement shape rather than per statement because the file is frozen: nothing new will be written here, so a broader anchor cannot mask a future finding. Remove this entry if the archive is ever deleted or rewritten.

The worked EXAMPLE of a CTE alias shadowing a physical table, quoted in the gate-4 section to explain why .sql files were removed from gate 1's prose derivation. The sentence's entire point is that `player_gamelogs` there is a WITH alias and `count` is its projection, so gate 1 reporting it is the illustration rather than a defect.

Real 42803, deliberately left failing pending an operator ruling on what the query is for. It projects nine per-game columns (targets, receiving_yards, rushing_attempts, ...) beside a count(*) under `group by year_week`, which is incoherent read either way: as a per-game listing the group by is wrong, as an occurrence count the nine columns are. Repairing it either direction would pick a meaning nobody has chosen. Remove this entry when the ruling lands and the query is rewritten.

Cited as an EXAMPLE of the false-positive class that keeps user-base .mjs out of gate 1's prose derivation: a JavaScript property read off a local variable whose name collides with the league `config` table. The sentence's whole point is that it is not a schema claim.

The league repo's own JS config object, read at libs-server/send-email.mjs module load (`config.email` gates whether the Resend client is built at all). `config` is a real league table, so this cannot be filtered by name -- same collision as config.databases and config.degraded above. Arrived with c6443c4c3, which documented why config-test.json enables mail.

Past-tense record, not live instruction. The sentence says a stale transactions.timestamp inside a concat_ws survived every gate, which is an accurate account of the defect 34a7a40f5 repaired -- the column is occurred_at now and the passage is the incident note explaining why gate 3 grew a .raw() transport. Naming the pre-rename spelling is the whole point of the sentence; rewriting it to occurred_at would make the paragraph describe a defect that could not have happened. Adjudicated 2026-08-08.

Not the league config table. This is a shell comment in user-base describing BASE's own config, whose machine_registry key is empty under NODE_ENV=test -- the environment validator-seams.mjs injects around. The league schema happens to carry a table called `config`, which is the only reason the prose pair rule binds the two halves together.

config.url is a property of this app's runtime config object (config.js, loaded per NODE_ENV), not the league config table -- that table is a key/value store whose only columns are key, config_value and updated_at. The sentence describes which base URL the emailed reset link is built from.

config.discord.channels is a dotted path into the USER-BASE config JSON, unrelated to the league database. The league config table is a key/value store (key, config_value, updated_at). Gate 1 binds the first two tokens because 'config' is also a real league table name.

config.discord.channels / config.discord.server_id are dotted paths into the USER-BASE config JSON consumed by extension/discord/lib/fetch-messages.mjs, not league columns. The league config table is a key/value store (key, config_value, updated_at).

Cited as one of five RECORDED INSTANCES of an audit rule missing a column -- history, not live instruction. The column has since been dropped from leagues (no %group% column remains), which does not falsify the example: the point being made is about the vocabulary gap in the audit rule, not about the column existing.
